system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: Ranking supermartingale

ATOM FPPROG-C04-S3-03 (S3): Soundness and completeness of RSM-maps for bounded termination does not make termination decidable, since it only guarantees the existence of an RSM-map of general form, which is not always computable; algorithmic synthesis therefore restricts the form (e.g. linear or polynomial) and can fail.

EVIDENCE:
[FPPROG-p0254-s03] The above soundness and completeness result does not imply that program termination is decidable, as it only ensures the existence of an RSM-map in general form which is not always computable.
[FPPROG-p0254-s08] Furthermore, since it is infeasible to synthesize an RSM-map in general form, in an algorithmic approach one needs to restrict the form of an RSM-map so as to make the approach feasible.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- GROUNDED: hold — Evidence supports nondecidability and restricting synthesis forms, but does not state linear/polynomial examples or that restricted synthesis can fail. / Drop '(e.g. linear or polynomial) and can fail', which is not stated in the cited evidence sentences.
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Combines nondecidability, noncomputability of general maps, restrictions on synthesis, and possible synthesis failure. / Joins two claims: why completeness does not imply decidability, and how algorithmic synthesis restricts the form of RSM-maps.
- L1_ONLY: hold — Retain the nondecidability limitation; remove the separate algorithmic-synthesis consequence and examples.
